items.q: What is Mike Krieger's core design-thinking loop?
items.a: **Identify problems, research, build, then validate** you actually solved them — the Stanford Symbolic Systems through-line from Instagram through Anthropic.

items.q: Why shouldn't you build in isolation for six months?
items.a: **Prototype early and show work along the way** so you catch fundamental errors before they harden. Everything you build should **solve a problem for somebody**.

items.q: How did Instagram know photo sharing was ready?
items.a: Kevin's location app Bourbon wasn't working; they stripped distractions and doubled down as **iPhone 3→4 camera jumps** and mobile networking improved — classic **technology readiness + rate of change**.

items.q: How should you build when the next model leap is coming?
items.a: **Build for today and catch the next wave** — useful now *and* architected for the next capability jump (cameras then, LLM leaps now).

items.q: What cold-start trap killed Artifact's personalization bet?
items.a: The product was great **after many articles**, but most users left after **two**, comparing it to Apple News. You must delight **before ML personalization kicks in**.

items.q: Why isn't smarter AI enough to win users?
items.a: **Intelligence alone is not product.** Users won't adopt features just because of the tech underneath — it still has to solve the problem from day one.

items.q: How do you know when to shut a startup down?
items.a: List untried ideas, run the top three, and if trajectory is unchanged, **check in with investors** — they're often ready before founders are. Failure is baked into VC, **not a tragedy**.

items.q: What makes AI product management uniquely hard?
items.a: **Products and models co-evolve** until about **a week before launch**. Claude's taste and artifacts shift with each model — a fundamentally dynamic stack.

items.q: How does Anthropic shape Claude's personality?
items.a: A **Claude character / vibes** team defines philosophy and tone; thumbs up/down (not conversation training) surfaces themes like verbosity for the next iteration.

items.q: What should onboarding make clear about AI limits?
items.a: Lead with **capabilities and failure modes** — models aren't doctors. Set the correct mental model at signup so users don't over-trust.

items.q: What kind of team beat siloed specialists at Instagram?
items.a: **Low-ego generalists** who care about the product — backend engineers ship iOS, PMs design — beat specialists waiting for strategy meetings.

items.q: What compounds more than any single project?
items.a: **Career relationships recur across decades.** Companies and projects change; the same people show up again — invest early.
